title: Testing & error handling
examples: When should I test my code?
What is the difference between a boundary test and an error test?
Can you give an example of using try except?

explain.say: We test our programs with different types of data.
Normal data is the typical input you expect to receive.
Boundary data tests the limits of what the program accepts.
Erroneous data is anything that breaks the program rules.
The try except structure helps manage these errors gracefully.

items: Except block: Run if error occurs

explain.say: For example, we try to divide by a number, but it might be zero.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of testing data?
faq.a: Testing data helps you find bugs before others do. It ensures your program works correctly under all conditions.
asks: Why do I need to test my code?
What is the goal of software testing?

faq.q: Can you explain boundary conditions better?
faq.a: Boundary conditions mean testing the absolute edges of acceptable values. You must test the smallest and largest allowed numbers.
asks: What are edge cases in programming?
How do I test the limits of input?

faq.q: When should I use the try except block?
faq.a: You use try except when you expect an operation might fail, like reading a file or dividing by a variable.
asks: How do I prevent my program from crashing?
What is error trapping in code?

faq.q: Is testing only for errors enough?
faq.a: No, you must also test normal cases and boundary cases. Only testing for errors is not enough for a good program.
asks: Do I need to test for success too?
What types of tests are there?

faq.q: What is the difference between an error and a boundary issue?
faq.a: An error is usually invalid data type, like text in a number field. A boundary issue is valid data, but too high or too low.

facts: Normal data represents typical, expected inputs for a program.
Boundary data tests the minimum and maximum acceptable values.
The try block contains code that might raise an exception.
The except block runs only if an exception occurs in the try block.

quiz.say: Which structure is used to attempt code that might fail?
quiz.why: The try keyword signals to the computer that the following code block should be monitored for errors.

wrong.0: Check is not a standard keyword for this type of error handling.
wrong.1: Validate is a general process, not a specific programming keyword.
wrong.3: Except runs only after an error happens, it does not attempt the code.

quiz.say: If a program tries to calculate the square root of a negative number, what type of test data is this?
quiz.why: Calculating the square root of a negative number results in an imaginary number, which is outside the expected real-number domain.

wrong.0: Normal data must be valid for the operation to succeed.
wrong.1: Boundary tests stick to the allowed range, not impossible mathematical operations.
wrong.2: Valid is too general; erroneous specifies the failure type.
